key_insight: Quantum circuit simulation cost is strongly family-dependent, so a family-aware residual model can predict approximation thresholds and runtime much better than a one-size-fits-all predictor.
engineering_relevance: This lets practitioners choose simulation settings in milliseconds instead of running expensive trial-and-error sweeps that can take minutes to hours.
method: Shared neural backbone encodes OpenQASM and execution context.
Pretrained family classifier provides algorithm-family conditioning.
Family-specific residual corrections add targeted adjustments using gate-composition fingerprint features.
evidence_signal: On circuits spanning 7–130 qubits across 10 families, the model reaches 79.5% exact threshold accuracy, 91.2% within one rung, and runtime prediction with R² = 0.82, with about 50 ms inference.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of family classification and on whether the training data covers the full range of circuit families and simulation contexts seen in deployment.
paper_title: Family-Aware Residual Architecture for Predicting Quantum Circuit Simulation Performance
